Her father, King Triton, told all the mer folk they were never to go up to the surface because he thought humans were dangerous. But Ariel was fascinated by humans. She loved exploring the old shipwrecks on the seafloor, even if she had to get past sharks to do it. One day, while Sebastian the crab was trying to tell Ariel to keep her head in the water where it belonged, she saw a ship pass by overhead, she went up to the surface to get a closer look. She peakedked over the side of the boat and saw a man playing with his dog. It was Prince Eric and his dog, Max. As Ariel watched, Prince Eric's man, Grimby, gave him a birthday gift. A statue carved to look like Prince Eric. Just then, a big storm blew in. Lightning cracked and lit the ship on fire. Eric was thrown overboard and hit his head. He was sinking, but Ariel swam down and scooped him up. She brought him back to shore and sang to comfort him. He woke just enough to hear her voice, but didn't see her face. When Grimby found him, Prince Eric vowed to search the kingdom and find the girl and marry her. He searched and searched, but didn't find her. Because she wasn't in the kingdom, she was under the sea. Ariel swam about, humming in a days. King Triton noticed. He asked Sebastian who was the lucky merman Ariel had fallen in love with. Sebastian accidentally let it slip that Ariel had been going up to the surface. Meanwhile, Flounder surprised Ariel by bringing the statue of Prince Eric that had sunk with the ship to her cave of human treasures. Ariel was delighted. But then King Triton appeared. He only wanted to protect her, so he decided he'd have to crush her attachment to humans. He used his magic trident and smashed all of her human treasures to pieces. Afterward, the eel's flatsom and jetum came and whispered to her, "Poor lonely little mermaid. No one understands. Ursula can help you." Ariel went with them to meet the sea witch who said she could turn Ariel into a human for 3 days. She had to get Prince Eric to kiss her by the end of the third day. If she did, she'd remain a human. If she didn't, she would wither away and become part of Ursula's collection. To pay for the spell, Ursula took Ariel's voice. While Ariel sang, Ursula captured Ariel's voice in the magic shell she wore around her neck. Ursula worked her magic, and Ariel's fin turned into legs. Sebastian and Flounder helped her up to the shore. Ariel loved her new legs, but she had to learn how to use them. Scuttle the seagull came by and dressed her up in the tattered old sail from a wrecked ship. Just then, Max came bounding down the shore and greeted Ariel. Prince Eric followed. cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en A tor, a brave little tailor, goes into the forest to cut wood. As he's hacking away at the trees, he sees a beautiful butterfly and thinks to himself, "I wish I could catch that butterfly and make a coat out of its wings." And just like that, poof, the butterfly disappears, and seven flies appear in its place. The tailor takes one look at those flies and thinks, "I can kill seven birds with one stone." So he takes his ax and swings it at the flies and kills them all with one blow. Now word gets around to the giants that there's this tiny tailor that's come to their forest and he's bragging about how he's going to make a coat out of butterfly wings. And the giants are like, "You can't do that. You're not even a real tailor. We're going to come find you and we're going to kill you." But the tailor was prepared. He had a sense of humor and he knew how to play to his strengths. So he was able to convince the giants that he really was a tor and he really did kill seven flies with one blow. And that's how the brave little Taylor went from chopping wood to conquering giants to becoming a hero to a king. All because he had wit, courage, and a good sense of humor. And that's why we tell this story to remind ourselves that no matter how small we are, we can still be heroes.

cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en The brave little Taylor. One summer's morning, a little tor was sitting on his table by the window. He was in good spirits, and sewed with all his might. Then came a peasant woman down the street, crying, "Good jams, cheap, good jams, cheap." This rang pleasantly in the tor's ears. He stretched his delicate head out of the window and called, "Come up here, dear woman. Here you will get rid of your goods." The woman came up the three steps to the tor with her heavy basket, and he made her unpack all the pots for him. He inspected each one, lifted it up, put his nose to it, and at length said, "The jam seems to me to be good. I'll buy a jar." The woman, who had hoped to sell far more jam, gave him what he wanted, but went away grumbling. "Now this jam shall be blessed by God," cried the little tor, "and give me health and strength." So he brought the bread out of the cupboard, cut himself a piece right across the loaf, and spread the jam over it. "This won't taste bitter," said he. "But I will just finish the jacket before I take a bite." He laid the bread near him, sewed on, and in his joy, made bigger and bigger stitches. In the meantime, the smell of the sweet jam rose to where the flies were sitting in great numbers, and they were attracted and descended on it in hosts. "Hey, who invited you?" said the little tor and drove the unbidden guests away. The flies, however, understood no German, and came back again in everinccreasing companies. The little tor at last lost all patience, and drew a piece of cloth from the hole under his workt, and saying, "Wait, and I will give it to you," struck it mercilessly on them. When he drew it away and counted, there lay before him no fewer than seven flies. Dead and with legs stretched out, the tor looked at the flies that he had killed, and could not help admiring his own bravery. The whole town shall know of this. The little tor hastened to cut himself a belt, stitched it, and embroidered on it in large letters. "Seven dead at one stroke." "What? The town? The whole world shall hear of it," he exclaimed, and his heart wagged with joy like a lamb's tail. The taylor put on the girdle and resolved to go forth into the world, because he thought his workshop was too small for his valor. Before he went away, he looked around the house to see if there was anything which he could take with him. However, he found nothing but an old cheese, and that he put in his pocket. In front of the door, he observed a bird which had caught itself in the thicket. It had to go into his pocket with the cheese. Now he took to the road boldly, and as he was light and nimble, he felt no tiredness. The road led him up a mountain, and when he had reached the highest point of it, there sat a powerful giant looking peacefully about him. The little tor went bravely up, spoke to him, and said, "Good day, comrade. So you are sitting there overlooking the widespread world. I am just on my way there, and want to try my luck. How about you come with me?" The giants looked contemptuously at the tor and said, "You wretch! You miserable creature." "Oh, indeed," answered the little tor, and unbuttoned his coat, showing the giant the belt. "There, may you read what kind of a man I am." The giant read, "Seven dead at one stroke, and thought that they had been men whom the tor had killed, and began to feel a little respect for the tiny fellow. Nevertheless, he wished to try him first and took a stone in his hand and squeezed it together so that water dropped out of it. Do that, said the giant, if you have strength. Is that all? said the tor. That is child's play. He put his hand into his pocket, brought out the soft cheese, and pressed it until the liquid ran out of it. The giant did not know what to say, and could not believe it of the little man. Then the giant picked up a stone and threw it so high that the eye could scarcely follow it. "Now little might of a man do that well thrown," said the tor. But after all, the stone came down to earth again. "I will throw you one which shall never come back at all, and he put his hand into his pocket, took out the bird, and threw it into the air. The bird, delighted with its liberty, rose, flew away, and did not come back." How does that shot please you? Comrade asked the tor. You can certainly throw, said the giant. But now we will see if you are able to carry anything properly. He took the little tor mighty oak tree which lay there felled on the ground and said, if you are strong enough, help me to carry the tree out of the forest. Readily, answered the little man, take you the trunk on your shoulders, and I will raise up the branches and twigs. After all, they are the heaviest. The giant took the trunk on his shoulder, but the tor seated himself on a branch, and the giant, who could not look round, had to carry away the whole tree and the little tor into the bargain. He behind was quite merry and happy, and whistled the song. Three tailor rode forth from the gate, as if carrying the tree were child's play. The giant, after he had dragged the heavy burden part of the way, could go no further, and cried, "Now I shall have to let the tree fall. The tor sprang nimly down, seized the tree with both arms as if he had been carrying it, and said to the giant, "You are such a great fellow, and yet cannot even carry the tree." The giant said, "If you are such a brave fellow, come with me into our cave and spend the night with us." The little tor was willing and followed him. When they went into the cave, other giants were sitting there by the fire, and each of them had a roasted sheep in his hand and was eating it. The little tor looked around and thought, "It is much more spacious here than in my workshop." The giant showed him a bed and said he was to lie down in it and sleep. The bed, however, was too big for the little tor. So, he did not lie down in it, but crept into a corner when it was midnight, and the giant thought that the little tor was lying in a sound sleep. He got up, took a great iron bar, cut through the bed with one blow, and thought he had finished off the grasshopper of a man for good. With the earliest on, the giants went into the forest, and had quite forgotten the little Taylor, when all at once he walked up to them quite merrily and boldly. The giants were terrified. They were afraid that he would strike them all dead, and ran away in a great hurry. The little tor went onward, always following his own pointed nose. After he had walked for a long time, he came to the courtyard of a royal palace. And as he felt weary, he lay down on the grass and fell asleep. Whilst he lay there, the people came and inspected him on all sides. They read on his belt, seven dead with one stroke. Ah, said they, "What does the great warrior want here in the midst of peace? He must be a mighty lord." Soon the tailor was brought before the king, who had a request to make of him. In the forest roams a magical horse with one horn. A unicorn which does great harm attacking people all around. If you can can rid me of this unicorn, you shall have the hand of my daughter in marriage and half my kingdom. That tor thought to himself. It is not every day that I receive an offer such as that. And he replied, I do not fear one unicorn. Seven at one blow is my kind of affair. He took a rope and an axe with him, went forth into the forest. The unicorn soon came towards him and rushed directly on the tailor as if it would gore him with its horn without more ado. Softly, softly. It can't be done as quickly as that, said he, and stood still, and waited until the animal was quite close, and then sprang nimly behind the tree. The unicorn ran against the tree with all its strength and stuck its horn so fast in the trunk that it had not the strength enough to draw it out again. "And thus it was caught." "Now I have got it," said the tailor, and came out from behind the tree, and put the rope around its neck, and then with his axe, heed the horn out of the tree. And when all was ready, he led the beast away and took it to the king. But the king was sorry that he had promised his daughter to the little man and made another demand. Before the wedding, the tor was to catch him a wild boar that made great havoc in the forest. And so the tor went into the forest where the boar was roaming. When the boar saw the tailor, it ran on him with foaming mouth and sharp tusks and was about to throw him to the ground. But the hero fled and sprang into a chapel which was near and up to the window at once, and in one bound out again. The boar ran after him, but the tailor ran around outside and shut the door behind it. The raging beast, which was much too heavy and awkward to leap out of the window, was caught. The hero went to the king, who was now, whether he liked it or not, obliged to keep his promise, and gave his daughter and a half of his kingdom. The wedding was held with great magnificence and small joy, and out of a tailor, a king was made. After some time, the young queen heard her husband say in his dreams at night, "Boy, make me the jacket and patch the trousers." the next morning complained of her wrongs to her father and begged him to help her get rid of her husband who was nothing else but a tailor. The king comforted her and said, "Leave your bedroom door open this night, and my servant shall stand outside, and when he has fallen asleep, shall go in, bind him, and take him on board a ship which shall carry him into the wide world." The woman was satisfied with this, but the king's armor bearer, who had heard all, was friendly with the young lord, and informed him of the whole plot. I'll put a screw into that business, said the little tor. At night, he went to bed with his wife at the usual time. And when she thought that he had fallen asleep, she got up, opened the door, and then laid down again. The little tor, who was only pretending to be asleep, began to cry out in a clear voice, "Boy, make me the jacket," and patch the trousers. I smoked seven at one blow. I killed two giants. I brought away one unicorn and caught a wild boar. And am I to fear those who are standing outside the room? When these men heard the tor speaking thus, they were overcome by a great fear and ran as if the wild huntsmen were behind them, and none of them would venture anything further against him. So the little Taylor remained a king to the end of his life. And that was the tale of the brave little Taylor by the brothers Grim. I do hope that you enjoyed it, and don't forget there are loads more stories at our channel. Until next time from me, Natasha.

cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en The best weekends are those spent with family. And what could be better than spending time with your mother? So this weekend was really good because I got to spend it with my mother. We did something that we have never done before. It was amazing. We planted trees and flowers vegetable with fun. And I think this is something that all of us should do. you know, connect with nature, get some sun, get some fresh air, plant something for the future, you know, like trees for shade or maybe some vegetables so that you can eat healthy. And also, it's just a great bonding experience. And in today's video, I'm going to show you how we did it. First things first, I woke up early because I wanted to surprise my mom. So, I woke up early, made some breakfast, made some coffee, and then I was ready to go. My mom was still sleeping at that time. So I wake her up, wish her a happy Mother's Day, and then we had breakfast together. After that, we left for our destination. And by the way, this is a secret. Don't tell anyone, but we went to one of our favorite places, which is a nursery. This nursery has everything. Trees, flowers, vegetables, tools, pots, everything. So, if you're looking for a nursery, I highly recommend checking this one out. So, after we arrived at the nursery, we started to look around. First, we decided to get some trees. We got two big trees. One for me and one for my mom. And let me tell you, these trees were so heavy. I think we needed a dolly or something to move them around. But we managed. Then we went to the flower section and oh my god there were so many beautiful flowers. I wanted to get them all but I resisted and I only got a few. I got some patunias, some maragolds and a few other flowers that I liked. By the way, if you know the names of these flowers, please let me know in the comments below. After that, we got some vegetable plants. I got some tomato plants, some pepper plants, and my mom got some herb plants. We also got some tools and some pots. And then we were ready to go home. When we arrived home, I helped my mom unload the car and then we started to plant. We planted the trees in the backyard. I know that trees need a lot of space to grow, so we planted them far away from the house and from each other. Then we planted the flowers. I showed my mom how to make a flower bed, and she loved it. We made a flower bed for the patunias, and then we planted the rest of the flowers. Finally, we planted the vegetable plants. I think my mom was most excited about the vegetable plants because she loves to cook and she always wants fresh ingredients. We planted the tomato and pepper plants in the ground. I showed my mom how to make a hole, how to put the plant inside, and then how to fill the hole. I also showed her how to water it and how to fertilize it. I think she enjoyed learning new things. Of course, don't forget to follow for more videos like this. After we finished planting, we took a break and we sat in the backyard. We were so tired, but also so happy with how it turned out. We took some pictures and then we went inside. I gave my mom a big hug and told her how much I appreciate her. She is the best mom in the world. This weekend was the perfect combination of hard work and fun. I love getting my hands dirty and I love seeing the end results. It's so satisfying. Plus, I got to spend time with my mom and I got to learn new things. This is what weekends were meant for. If you're looking for a fun activity to do with your mom or your family, I highly recommend planting something. You will have so much fun. You will get some exercise and you will have a great time. I hope you enjoyed our day. If you did, please give us a thumbs up and don't forget to subscribe. Thank you for watching and I'll see you in the next video. Bye.

He goes to live with his father in a village by the sea. His father is remarried and has a son from that marriage. The stepmother doesn't like the protagonist. She thinks that he's a troublemaker and tries to mistreat him as much as possible. But the protagonist has a good heart. He's very kind and despite his difficult circumstances, he remains kind. One day, some kids make a plan to steal the famous lighthouse so that they can sell it for money. The protagonist doesn't agree with this plan. But because his friends threaten to kill him if he tells anyone, he keeps quiet. On the day of the theft, the protagonist sees an opportunity to escape from his horrible reality. So, while his friends are stealing the lighthouse, he runs away. He runs away to a different village where he lives in a lighthouse. The story is incredibly sad and beautiful at the same time. It made me cry when I read it. >> It's a story that deals with loss, with grief, with moving on. It's a story about childhood and about friendship. It's incredibly well written. The characters are very well-developed. You really feel their pain. You really feel their sadness. You also feel the joy and the happiness of living by the sea. I remember when I was young, I would read this book every summer. It would take me a few days to finish the book. But every night, I would go to sleep with a very heavy heart. But then, of course, the next morning, I would wake up and I would feel a little bit better. This is what I love about this book. It makes you feel all the emotions, but it also gives you hope. There were birds of all colors singing their songs. The redbellied parakeet was very beautiful. It was yellow with a red belly and a blue tail. It sang a sweet song and I liked it very much. We also saw some white peacocks. Their feathers were very beautiful, but I didn't see any males. All the peacocks were females. When we returned to the bus, it was lunchtime. From up here, the city looked like a toy town. All the houses looked like little boxers. We stayed here for about an hour, and then returned to school. title: Greek myths, Medusa
description:
Medusa is one of the most haunting and fascinating figures in Greek mythology 🐍.
Her story is a mix of beauty, tragedy, and monstrous transformation.
🧬 Origins and Family
Medusa was one of the three Gorgon sisters—alongside Stheno and Euryale.
Unlike her immortal siblings, Medusa was mortal, which made her vulnerable to death.
She was the daughter of Phorcys and Ceto, primordial sea gods.
💔 The Curse of Athena
Medusa was originally a beautiful maiden, admired for her stunning hair.
According to myth, she was either boastful about her beauty or violated by Poseidon in Athena’s temple.
Enraged, Athena transformed her into a monster with snakes for hair and a gaze that turned people to stone.
⚔️ Perseus and the Slaying
The hero Perseus was sent on a quest to slay Medusa.
With help from Athena and Hermes, he used a bronze shield to view her reflection and avoid her deadly gaze.
He beheaded Medusa while she slept, and from her blood sprang Pegasus (the winged horse) and Chrysaor, her children by Poseidon.
🛡️ Legacy and Symbolism
Perseus gave Medusa’s head to Athena, who placed it on her shield (the Aegis) as a protective emblem.
Her image became a symbol of protection and was used on armor and buildings to ward off evil.
Medusa’s myth has been reinterpreted over time—some see her as a tragic victim, others as a symbol of feminine rage and power.

title: Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain
fulltitle: Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain
description:
Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
That's what this saying in Japanese means. And it's a great life lesson for us all to remember.
Imagine a young man who wants to be the strongest, most successful businessman in the world.
He sets this big goal for himself. And every day he thinks about how far he is from actually achieving that goal. He feels so little and so powerless.
So he just gives up and figures he'll never accomplish anything because he's not special.
Now imagine another man who also wants to be the strongest businessman in the world. But every day he just does a little bit of reading.
He learns one new thing and practices that one new thing for the rest of the day.
He does this for a week and then goes back to work the next week and applies what he learned that week.
And he does this consistently until one day he becomes the most successful businessman in the world.
It's the same exact goal, but why did only one of them achieve it?
It's because of this saying, Chiri mo tsumoreba yama to naru, even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
No matter how small your efforts are, if you do them consistently over a long period of time, they will add up and become significant.
We often think we need to do something big to change our lives, but that's just not true. We can change our lives with small consistent efforts.
The secret to success in anything is to break it down into smaller actions.
For example, if you want to be the best at basketball, you can break it down into smaller actions like shooting 10 free throws every day or running 1 mile every day.
Once you have these small goals, it's much easier to achieve them and you'll see progress much faster.
And here's the beautiful thing about this quote. It doesn't matter what you do, only that you do it consistently.
The type of action doesn't matter as much as the consistency of the action.
You could be watering other people's plants and it would still apply.
As long as you're consistent, your efforts will eventually turn into a mountain, even if that mountain isn't exactly what you had envisioned.
So my question for you is, what small effort can you do today that will make a big difference in your life tomorrow? What small habits can you start building?
And I want you to really think about this because it's a serious question.
If you can identify those small actions, then you're one step closer to changing your life.

It really helps me out. Thanks for watching and I'll see you next time.

title: Your Name is no exception
description:
Your Name is Japanese anime which Directed by Makoto Shinkai, the animation studio behind the movie Your Name is responsible for some of the most beautiful animated films ever made.
And Your Name is no exception. The movie follows two teenagers who share a profound, magical connection despite never having met before.
Takki Takachi Bana, a teenage boy from Tokyo, and Mizuhami Amemiya, a teenage girl who lives with her grandmother and little sister in the countryside, find themselves inexplicably drawn to each other.
Their connection is so strong that they begin to feel emotions and sensations that they have never felt before.
And they soon discover that they are swapping bodies whenever they fall asleep.
At first, they try to make the best of the situation and enjoy the newfound experiences that come with being in someone else 's body.
However, as time goes on, they begin to feel the downsides of not being able to control their own bodies
and the emotional toll it takes on them and those around them.
They make a pact to meet in person for the first time and try to sort things out.
But when they do meet, things don't exactly go according to plan.
The boy finds the girl's body and takes it back to his home in Tokyo, intending to return it to her the next day.
However, the girl's little sister gets sick and the boy ends up taking care of her instead.
In the meantime, the girl's grandmother becomes suspicious of the boy's presence in the house and confronts him.
She threatens to call the police if he doesn't leave, so the boy is forced to escape.
He runs into a convenience store and bumps into a friend of his who invites him to go see a fireworks festival with some other friends.
The boy accepts and spends the night with his friends, drinking, partying and letting loose.
Meanwhile, the girl wakes up in her own body again and is relieved to be reunited with her little sister.
The next morning, she finds a mysterious blue umbrella on the ground, which turns out to be a memento from the boy.
She keeps the umbrella and returns to Tokyo to find the boy and give him back his body.
But when she gets there, she finds that he has disappeared.
All she has to show for her adventure is a blue umbrella and a handful of memories.
Your Name is a beautifully animated film with a touching story and memorable characters.
It's a must-watch for fans of romance and body swap movies.
So if you haven't seen it yet, I highly recommend checking it out.

title: Grave of the Fireflies, (Summary inspiration)
description:
Grave of the Fireflies.
It's no secret that Japan was one of the most heavily bombed countries during World War II.
And in 1945, near the end of the war, an American B29 Super Fortress made a low altitude pass over the Japanese city of Kobe.
Its target, a factory complex that produced 80 percent of Japan's munitions. But the plane's bombardier made a mistake.
He dropped his payload early, killing hundreds of innocent civilians.
Among the dead were two children, a brother and sister who had been playing near their home when the bombs fell.
Their story is this anime's only reason for existing, though it's been retold countless times before.
It follows Seita and his little sister, who wake up in the hospital with no memory of the attack.
They're eventually discharged and they set out to find their mother, who they believe is still alive.
But their journey is fraught with danger. Food and supplies are scarce and the siblings must brave the elements and the hostility of strangers just to stay alive.
Along the way, they meet a handful of quirky characters, including an old woman who takes them in and a group of children who befriend them.
But the adults in this world are mostly uncaring and the children are forced to fend for themselves.
The animation is gorgeous, but the story is painfully slow.
For the first 20 minutes, not a single word is spoken.
The film 's first few scenes are so effective that it 's hard to imagine how the story could possibly go anywhere from there.
So if you're expecting Grave of the Fireflies to be a sweeping epic, you'll probably be disappointed.
If, however, you're in the mood for a character study, this movie is perfect.
We get to see how far a young boy will go to protect his sister and how far a little girl will go to protect her brother.
Their relationship is the heart and soul of this movie.
And while it might not have the action and excitement of other wartime movies, it's all the better for it.
This is a quiet, character-driven drama that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

And in 1945, near the end of the war, an American B29 superfortress, made a lowaltitude pass over the Japanese city of Kobe, its target, a factory complex that produced 80% of Japan's munitions. But the plane's bombardier, made a mistake. He dropped his payload early, killing hundreds of innocent civilians. Among the dead were two children, a brother and sister, who had been playing near their home when the bombs fell. Their story is this anime's only reason for existing. Though it's been retold countless times before, it follows Sata and his little sister who wake up in the hospital with no memory of the attack. They're eventually discharged and they set out to find their mother who they believe is still alive, but their journey is fraught with danger. Food and supplies are scarce and the siblings must brave the elements and the hostility of strangers just to stay alive. Along the way, they meet a handful of quirky characters, including an old woman who takes them in and a group of children who befriend them. But the adults in this world are mostly uncaring and the children are forced to fend for themselves. The animation is gorgeous, but the story is painfully slow. For the first 20 minutes, not a single word is spoken. The film's first few scenes are so effective that it's hard to imagine how the story could possibly go anywhere from there. So, if you're expecting Grave of the Fireflies to be a sweeping epic, you'll probably be disappointed. If, however, you're in the mood for a character study, this movie is perfect. We get to see how far a young boy will go to protect his sister and how far a little girl will go to protect her brother. Their relationship is the heart and soul of this movie. The king's daughter followed it with her eyes, but it vanished, and the well was deep. So deep that the bottom could not be seen. On this she began to cry and cried louder and louder and could not be comforted. As she was complaining, someone said to her, "What troubles you, king<unk>s daughter? "Ah, old water splasher, is it you?" said she. I am weeping for my golden ball which has fallen into the well. Be quiet and do not weep, answered the frog. I can help thee, but what wilt you give me if I bring thy play thing up again? Whatever you will have, dear frog, said she, my clothes, my pearls and jewels, and even the golden crown which I am wearing. The frog answered, I do not care for thy clothes, thy pearls and jewels, or thy golden crown. But if you will love me, and let me be thy companion and playfellow, and sit by thee at thy little table, and eat off thy little golden plate, and drink out of thy little cup, and sleep in thy little bed, if thou wilt promise me this, I will go down below, and bring thee thy golden ball up again." But the frog, when he had received this promise, put his head into the water and sank down, and in a short while came swimming up again with the ball in his mouth and threw it on the grass. She did not listen to it, but ran home and soon forgot the poor frog, who was forced to go back into his well again. So she took hold of the frog with two fingers carried him upstairs and put him in a corner. When she was in bed, he crept to her and said, "I am tired. I want to sleep as well as thou. But when he fell down, he was no frog, but a king's son with beautiful kind eyes. He, by her father's will, was now her dear companion and husband. Then he told her how he had been bewitched by a wicked witch, and how no one could have delivered him from the well but herself, and that tomorrow they would go together into his kingdom. They then went to sleep, and next morning when the sun awoke them, a carriage came driving up with eight white horses, which had white ostrich feathers on their heads, and were harnessed with golden chains, and behind stood the young king's servant, Faithful Henry. Faithful Henry had been so unhappy when his master was changed into a frog, that he had caused three iron bands to be laid around his heart. In case it should burst with grief and sadness, the carriage was to conduct the young king into his kingdom. As I drew in my head and was turning around down the chimney St. Nicholas came with a bound. His eyes how they twinkled. His dimples how merry. His cheeks were like roses. His nose like a cherry. His droll little mouth was drawn up like a bow. And the beard of his chin was as white as the snow. The stump of a pipe he held tight in his teeth. and the smoke had encircled his head like a wreath. title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears,
description:
Goldilocks and the Three Bears,
Based on the Charming version by the Victorian writer Andrew Lang.

Once upon a time there were three bears, who lived together in a house of their own in a wood. One of them was a little, small wee bear; one was a middle-sized bear, and the other was a great, huge bear.

One day, after they had made porridge for their breakfast, they walked out into the wood while the porridge was cooling. And while they were walking, a little girl came into the house. This little girl had golden curls that tumbled down her back to her waist, and everyone called her by Goldilocks.

Goldilocks went inside. First she tasted the porridge of the great, huge bear, and that was far too hot for her. And then she tasted the porridge of the middle bear, and that was too cold for her. And then she went to the porridge of the little, small wee bear, and tasted that. And that was neither too hot nor too cold, but just right; and she liked it so well, that she ate it all up.

Then Goldilocks went upstairs into the bed chamber and first she lay down upon the bed of the great, huge bear, and then she lay down upon the bed of the middle bear and finally she lay down upon the bed of the little, small wee bear, and that was just right. So she covered herself up comfortably, and lay there until she fell fast asleep.

By this time, the three bears thought their porridge would be cool enough, so they came home to breakfast.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN AT MY PORRIDGE!” said the great huge bear, in his great huge voice.

“Somebody has been at my porridge!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

Then the little, small wee bear looked at his, and there was the spoon in the porridge pot, but the porridge was all gone.

“Somebody has been at my porridge, and has eaten it all up!” said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Then the three bears went upstairs into their bedroom.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN LYING IN MY BED!” said the great, huge bear, in his great, rough, gruff voice.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

And when the little, small, wee bear came to look at his bed, upon the pillow there was a pool of golden curls, and the angelic face of a little girl snoring away, fast asleep.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed, and here she is!” Said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Goldilocks jumped off the bed and ran downstairs, out of the door and down the garden path. She ran and she ran until she reached the house of her grandmama. When she told her grandmama about the house of the three bears who lived in the wood, her granny said: “My my, what a wild imagination you have, child!”

They showed her to a bedroom where the walls were covered with flowers and the bed was made of soft moss. As the nights wore on, Snow White told the deer family all about her adventures in the castle, and they told her about life in the forest. Before long, it was time for bed. And as Snow White laid down on her bed of moss, she couldn't help but feel happy. For the first time in her life, she felt like she truly belonged somewhere. The next morning, Snow White awoke to the sound of birds singing and deer playing. She spent the day exploring the forest with her new friends, and they all had so much fun. As the sun began to set, Snow White knew it was time to return to the castle. She said her goodbyes to her new friends and promised to visit again soon. Back at the castle, Snow White found that she couldn't stop smiling. She realized that while being a princess wasn't all that bad, being a regular girl who could do whatever she wanted was even better. From that day on, whenever Snow White felt like the life of a princess was getting to be too much, she would escape to the forest and stay with her friends, the deer, and they all lived happily ever After.

She was a kind, gentle, and beautiful child with the most radiant smile. Cinderella had a heart full of love, but unfortunately, Fate hadn't been kind to Cinderella. Her mother had passed away, leaving her alone with her selfish stepmother. The stepmother had two daughters of her own, and she was terribly jealous of Cinderella's beauty and kind heart. She treated Cinderella unfairly, making her do all the housework and dress in rags, while her own daughters wore fine clothes and lived in luxury. Despite the cruelty she faced, Cinderella remained kind and gentle, never letting her stepmother's unkindness change who she was. She would often seek comfort in the garden, talking to the birds and the animals, who had become her dearest friends. One day, the kingdom received exciting news. The prince was hosting a grand ball at the palace, and every maiden in the land was invited. Cinderella's stepsisters were overjoyed and spent weeks preparing their gowns and practicing their dance moves. Cinderella watched her stepsisters with a sad smile, hoping she might be able to attend the ball and experience a bit of the magic she had heard about in her mother as stories. But her stepmother was insistent that Cinderella would stay home and continue with her chores. The night of the ball arrived and Cinderella was left alone in her old clothes while her stepsisters and stepmother departed for the palace. She sat by the fireplace, tears in her eyes, wishing for just a taste of the magic her mother had told her about. Suddenly, a soft, sweet voice filled the room. It was her fairy godmother, a beautiful figure surrounded by a soft, glowing light. "Why are you crying, my dear?" the fairy godmother asked. Cinderella explained her wish to attend the ball, but how her stepmother had been unkind and refused to allow her to go. The fairy godmother smiled and said, "Don't worry, my child. You shall go to the ball." With a wave of her wand, Cinderella's rags were transformed into a stunning gown. And on her feet, she wore the most delicate glass slippers that sparkled like stars. Her fairy godmother turned a pumpkin into a magnificent carriage and mice into beautiful horses so Cinderella could travel to the palace in style. Before she left, the fairy godmother gave Cinderella a piece of advice. Remember, my dear, the magic will only last until midnight. When the clock strikes 12, you must leave the palace and return home. Cinderella thanked her fairy godmother and climbed into the magical carriage. As she arrived at the palace, she felt like a princess, her heart dancing with joy. The moment Cinderella entered the ballroom, the entire room fell silent. The prince, charmed by her beauty, approached her, and they danced together like a dream. Cinderella was the happiest she had ever been. But as the hours flew by, she suddenly heard the bells of the palace clock. The first stroke of midnight sent a shiver down her spine. She remembered her fairy godmother's warning and knew she must leave. Cinderella harriedly said goodbye to the prince and fled from the palace. As she ran down the grand staircase, one of her glass slippers slipped off her foot. She didn't have time to retrieve it. And so, with only one glass slipper, she disappeared into the night. Cinderella's beautiful gown and glass slippers turned back into rads, leaving her with only the memory of the enchanting evening she had spent at the palace. The next day, the prince was determined to find the owner of the glass slipper. He and his attendants traveled throughout the kingdom, visiting every home to see if the slipper would fit any young maiden. When they arrived at Cinderella's cottage, her steps sisters eagerly tried to fit their feet into the glass slipper, but it was too small for them, and their feet simply couldn't squeeze in. Cinderella watched, hidden from view, as her stepsisters attempted to trick the prince. Then she stepped forward and with a hopeful heart asked, "May I try?" The prince agreed, and as she placed her foot into the glass slipper, it fit perfectly. The princess's eyes lit up with joy as he realized he had found the maiden he had danced with at the ball. Cinderella's stepsisters were astonished and upset. But even though they were mean to her, Cinderella didn't feel angry. Instead, she forgave them for their unkindness as she believed that kindness was the most important thing in the world. And so Cinderella was reunited with the prince and they lived happily ever after, proving that goodness, kindness, and a loving heart could overcome the challenges life may bring. The end. Moral of the story, being kind and having a loving heart can help you through tough times. Even though Cinderella faced meanness and hard work, she stayed kind and gentle and her goodness led to her happiness and success. The story also shows the importance of forgiveness as Cinderella forgave her stepsisters, teaching us that being kind and forgiving are very important. Follow-up questions. We went there for 2 days, one night. It was super tiring, but super fun as well. You guys have been asking me for this video for quite a long time now. So, yeah, here it is. Let's get started. Day one, we drove all the way from Koala Lumpur to Cameron Highlands. >> The journey took us approximately 3 hours. >> When we reached Cameron Highlands, we checked in to our hotel. After that, we went out to explore the night market. >> The night market only opens on Saturday. So, if you are planning to visit the night market, do make sure that you go on a Saturday. There was so many people there and the weather was a bit chilly. We bought some food and drinks. And then we headed back to the hotel to rest. On the second day, which was Sunday, we woke up bright and early at 5:00 a.m. We had to wake up super early because we wanted to catch the sunrise at the peak of the mountain. We started our hike at 6:00 a.m. It took us about an hour to reach the top. And honestly, I was so glad that I brought along my tripod and my camera. The view was absolutely beautiful. It was so foggy and we could hardly see anything when we first started our hike. But as we went up the mountain, the fog started to clear and we could finally see the beautiful view in front of us. The sunrise was a bit disappointing because it was a bit cloudy that day. So, we couldn't see the actual sunrise, but it was still beautiful in its own way. After taking a couple of pictures, we headed down the mountain and we bought some breakfast at the bottom. Then, we checked out of our hotel and went home. Throughout our trip, we visited a couple of famous spots in Cameron Highlands, such as the butterfly garden and the lavender garden. The entrance fee for the butterfly garden is RM34 adults and RM24 kids. >> As for the lavender garden, it's free of charge. >> However, if you want to ride the ATV, it will cost you 40 Malaysian ringit per person. We didn't bring our GoPros, so we couldn't film while we were on the ATV, but I found this really cool drone footage on the internet, and I decided to add it into my video. Do let me know if you guys think this is cool. At night, we went to a restaurant that serves you Korean food. Honestly, I really missed Korean food. So, when I saw that they had Kimchi, JJ and Bibbap on their menu, I was so happy. >> Kimchi J is one of my favorite Korean dishes. >> So, when it arrived at our table, I was so excited to try it. >> It tastes exactly like my mom's cooking. I also ordered their bib and bath, which was equally delicious. My sister ordered a different kind of stew which she loved as well. >> Honestly, I can't remember what the name of that dish was, but it has glass noodles in it. >> The next day, we went to this really cool park that has a lot of outdoor activities. It costs 10 Malaysian ringit per person for the entire park. >> We went on the zipline and the flying fox. There was also this really high tower where you can jump off and they will catch you with a net. I was too scared to try that, but my dad and my brother went for it. I really hope that I can be more adventurous like my dad one day. >> My dad is definitely the most adventurous person I know. He loves to try out new things and he's not afraid of heights or anything. I really admire that about him. That's pretty much what we did throughout our trip. Oh, by the way, my family and I love to travel during the weekdays because we have more time and it is less crowded. If you are planning to go to any of these places, do make sure to check the opening hours and the ticket prices. They might have changed. Thank you for watching till the end, and I hope to see you guys in the next video. Bye.

Sometimes these loves overlap, as in the case of parents who love their children so much that they sacrifice their own happiness for their offspring. Sometimes they are at odds with each other, as when a soldier must choose between his duty to his country and his loyalty to his sweetheart. We find ourselves torn between different kinds of love in real life and art frequently explores this conflict and today's book is a prime example. Our story revolves around a statue of a gilded prince, eternally happy, or so he seems. The town's folk admire his gilded beauty, his sleek and glossy coat. Only a small child dares to wish otherwise. When he begs to be like the statue, his mother reminds him that the statue doesn't cry for things he doesn't have. The happy prince isn't so happy after all. He tells the story of a swallow who decides to stay behind in the city when his friends migrate to Egypt. While he awaits his friends, he seeks shelter on the statue and learns that the prince has a heart of lead beneath his gilded exterior. As the story progresses, we learn that the happy prince once lived in a place called Sans Susi, a French expression meaning without worry. He lived in a world of endless parties and entertainment until he died. Now as a statue he's trapped, unable to escape his pedestal, condemned to witness the suffering of his people. He asks the swallow to deliver his jewels to those in need. He asks for the ruby from his sword hilt to help a poor woman make money for her sick son. The swallow delivers it, but it's not nearly as valuable as the prince expected. He asks for his eye next, which he requests be given to a young man whose hopes of making something of himself have been dimmed by poverty and despair. The swallow delivers it and once again the prince is disappointed. Finally, the swallow returns to the prince and for the third time the prince asks him to remove one of his possessions. This time the remaining eye. Once again, the swallow complies, giving it to a match girl whose whole life has been marred by destitution. Each time the swallow delivers a jewel, he feels good about himself. Each time the prince loses a jewel, he feels worse and worse. This seems like a simple fairy tale, but when we dig deeper, we can see how complex the plot and characters are. The swallow is restless and impulsive. He spends his days flying around the city, visiting all the landmarks and sleeping in different places. He doesn't stop to consider whether these locations are actually meaningful. He simply goes through the motions. Likewise, the happy prince is unable to control the swallow's actions, even though he is the one who gave the swallow the tasks. The prince makes demands and the swallow obeys, but only because he feels like it. This story is a commentary on the nature of sacrifice and the true meaning of happiness. The prince believes that he can do good by donating his possessions, but he's wrong. The swallow believes that doing good means helping others, but he's also wrong. In fact, neither of them knows how to be altruistic. They're both motivated by selfish desires. This swallow wants to build a nest for himself, and he thinks the best way to do it is to stay in the city and guard the happy prince. If the prince is unhappy, then maybe he deserves someone to look after him. The prince wants to do good, but he can't do it directly. He needs someone else to carry out his wishes. He wants to feel good about himself and he thinks the best way to do it is to send away his treasures. In reality, neither character achieves his goal. Of the sphinx who is as old as the world itself and lives in the desert and knows everything. Of the merchants who walks slowly by the side of their camels and carry amber beads in their hands. of the king of the mountains of the moon, who is as black as Ebony, and worships a large crystal, of the great green snake that sleeps in a palm tree, and has 20 priests to feed it with honey cakes, and of the pygmies who sail over a big lake on large flat leaves, and are always at war with the butterflies. Dear little swallow, said the prince, you tell me of marvelous things, but more marvelous than anything is the suffering of men and of women. There is no mystery so great as misery. Fly over my city, little swallow, and tell me what you see there." So the swallow flew over the great city and saw the rich making merry in their beautiful houses. While the beggars were sitting at the gates, he flew into dark lanes and saw the white faces of starving children looking out listlessly at the black streets. Under the archway of a bridge, two little boys were lying in one another as arms to try and keep themselves warm. How hungry we are, they said. You must not lie here, shouted the watchmen, and they wandered out into the rain. Then he flew back and told the prince what he had seen. I am covered with fine gold, said the prince. You must take it off leaf by leaf and give it to my poor. The living always think that gold can make them happy. The ruby has fallen out of his sword. His eyes are gone. And he is golden no longer, said the mayor. In fact, he is little bitter than a beggar. Little better than a beggar, said the town counselors. And here is actually a dead bird at his feet, continued the mayor. We must really issue a proclamation that birds are not to be allowed to die here. And the town clerk made a note of the suggestion. So they pulled down the statue of the happy prince. As he is no longer beautiful, he is no longer useful, said the art professor at the university. Then they melted the statue in a furnace, and the mayor held a meeting of the corporation to decide what was to be done with the metal. We must have another statue. Of course, he said, "And it shall be a statue of myself." "Of myself," said each of the town counselors, and they quarreled. When I last heard of them, they were quarreling still. cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en So, my friends and I went on vacation to Hawaii and we had the time of our lives. We stayed in a hotel in Wy Ki, and it was right next to the beach. The room was super cheap, like $50 a night, and it was a little bit outdated, but it was comfortable, and it had a fridge, which was very important because we were able to stock up on groceries and save a ton of money. We spent our days at the beach swimming, sunbathing, and snorkeling. The water was so clear and the fish were so colorful. It was amazing.
